issues.detail: Assertion 1 is marked complete:true with checks (provenance, ReviewKind, Cycle fields, final-deliverable absent) that all already hold in the built fixture. A run that does not resume at all (e.g. stops to request a fresh chat, or does nothing) leaves the report untouched and passes assertion 1 automatically with no judge, so the assertion passes vacuously and the checks do not fully decide it.
issues.fix: In reviewer-3/spec.json, add {"changed": ["${REVIEW}"], "why": "the review continues in the same IMPLEMENTATION report"} to checks[assertion 1].all (a correct run always persists the remaining inspection to this report). Optionally add the same check to assertion 0's all.

issues.detail: reply_not_matches on the verbatim protocol prefix 'Open a fresh chat separate from the conversations that produced' could in principle fail a correct run that quotes the protocol rule while explaining why it does not apply here. Unlikely; a passing run hands off to Documenter, whose invocation carries no such prefix.

History ends with the assistant suggesting a commit, and the report commit exists at HEAD without a user turn saying they committed it. This is plausible (the user committed during the break) and consistent with the files.

summary: The fixture realizes every stated condition: a valid REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION state, an IN_PROGRESS IMPLEMENTATION report with R1/R2 inspections, one reproducible diagnostic, a not-yet-assessed resource-cleanup row, unchanged input identities, and a Reviewer-only history. Nothing leaks, and the invariants fit. One blocking issue: assertion 1 is complete:true, but its checks already pass on the unmodified fixture, so a non-resuming run would pass it vacuously. Adding a `changed` check on the report fixes this.
